question: What is the ICAO Aerodrome Reference Code of the A320neo?
reference: The A320neo is classified as ICAO Aerodrome Reference Code 3C.

question: When is an A320-200 classified as ICAO aerodrome code 4C instead of 3C?
reference: When its take-off weight is more than 73 500 kg (162 040 lb); at or below 73 500 kg it is code 3C.

question: How does the Boeing 787 differ from earlier airplanes in its pneumatic system?
reference: It has a more-electric design without a traditional pneumatic system: engine starters are gearbox-mounted starter/generators, cabin air conditioning and wing anti-ice are electric, and the remaining pneumatic system is only for engine nacelle anti-ice.

question: How many fatal accidents did the worldwide commercial jet fleet have in 2016-2025 according to Boeing's Statistical Summary?
reference: 31 fatal accidents.

question: According to Boeing's Statistical Summary, what share of fatal accidents in 2016-2025 happened during landing, and how much flight time does landing represent?
reference: Landing accounted for 35% of fatal accidents while representing only about 1% of flight time.

question: What is the Soft Go-Around function introduced by Airbus?
reference: A safety enhancement that provides reduced go-around thrust (instead of full TOGA) when all engines are operating, targeting a climb rate of 2000 or 2300 ft/min depending on the model; TOGA must still be used with an engine inoperative and can be selected at any time.

question: When did Airbus start publishing a dedicated safety magazine, and when did it become 'Safety First'?
reference: Airbus started with 'Hangar Flying' in June 1995; it was renamed Safety First in 2004 and the first Safety First issue came out in January 2005.

question: Which has the larger lower-deck cargo volume, the Boeing 737-10 or the Boeing 787-8, and by roughly how much?

question: Compare the usable fuel capacity of the A320neo with that of the 737 MAX (no auxiliary tanks). Which carries more?

question: Compare the single-class seating capacity of the A320 and the Boeing 737-8.

Are the A320neo and the 737 MAX in the same ICAO aerodrome reference code letter?
reference: Yes. Both are code letter C: the A320neo is code 3C and the 737 MAX remains an ICAO Aerodrome Reference Code letter C (FAA Airplane Design Group III) aircraft.

question: Which engine manufacturers power the Boeing 787 and the Airbus A320neo?
reference: 787: General Electric and Rolls-Royce engines. A320neo: Pratt & Whitney (PW1100G) and CFM International (LEAP-1A). Each aircraft offers two engine manufacturers.

question: Compare the maximum design landing weight of the Boeing 787-8 with the maximum landing weight of the A320-200.
reference: 787-8: 380,000 lb (172,365 kg); A320-200 (most weight variants): 64 500 kg (142 198 lb), so the 787-8 landing weight is roughly 2.7 times higher.

question: What are the main safety themes discussed across the Airbus Safety First magazines?
reference: Flight operations (non-precision instrument approaches, soft go-around, energy management, control inputs in manual flight), training crews for unexpected events, cabin safety (proper seating), correct use of the MEL, ground operations and cargo fire protection, and the industry-wide safety strategy (Destination 10X, sharing safety information).

question: How do the Airbus and Boeing documents describe the overall trend in commercial aviation safety?
reference: Both describe accidents at historically low levels while traffic keeps growing: Boeing reports large declines between the last two decades (accident rate -35%, hull loss rate -58%, fatal accident rate -60%); Airbus notes fatal accidents are historically low but flat per flight, so traffic growth (doubling over 15 years) means the industry must further enhance safety and share safety information.

question: What kinds of information do the airport-planning manuals from Airbus and Boeing provide?
reference: Standardized airport planning data: aircraft description and general characteristics (design weights, seating, cargo volume, fuel), dimensions and ground clearances, interior arrangements and doors, aircraft performance (payload-range, takeoff and landing field length), ground maneuvering (turning radii), terminal servicing, jet wake/noise and pavement data.

question: Summarize the main features of the Boeing 737 MAX family described in its planning manual.
reference: Models 737-7, -8, -8-200, -9, -10 plus Business Jet versions; improved fuel efficiency, more payload/range, lower emissions and noise; new CFM LEAP-1B engines; Advanced Technology dual-feather winglets; remains FAA Design Group III / ICAO code C.

question: Which design weight terms are used by both manufacturers and what do they mean?
reference: Both define maximum design taxi/ramp weight (max for ground manoeuvre incl. taxi fuel), maximum design takeoff weight (max at start of takeoff run), maximum design landing weight, and maximum design zero fuel weight (max weight without usable fuel), all limited by structural strength and airworthiness requirements; plus seating capacity, cargo volume and usable fuel.
